Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it.  Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.

We work with over 5,000+ teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to help build, operate and improve the infrastructure, platforms and tools that enable our teams to develop, deliver and run reliable software at scale.

Based in Cologne, you will join a team with broad ownership of our technical environment. We take a cloud-agnostic approach, combining cloud services and self-hosted infrastructure to meet the needs of our products and engineering teams. Our responsibilities span the full lifecycle, from provisioning and deployment to observability, security and ongoing operation.

You will combine infrastructure expertise with automation and software engineering to improve how our software is built, deployed and operated. This includes streamlining development workflows, integrating and maintaining shared tools, and supporting demanding workloads across data processing, media and machine learning. Working closely with engineering teams and colleagues across the business, you will build practical solutions that support our expanding product portfolio.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving a wide range of technical problems, takes ownership from initial idea through to production, and thrives in a fast-growing environment where priorities and requirements evolve quickly. You will help shape how our infrastructure, platforms and tools adapt as the business grows.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Design, operate, and continuously improve our Kubernetes platform across both self-hosted clusters and AWS
  • Own our infrastructure as code using Terraform and Ansible, driving a GitOps workflow to ensure all changes are versioned, reviewed, and reproducible
  • Build and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI) and shared templates that empower product teams to build, test, and deploy reliably
  • Operate and scale specialized infrastructure for demanding workloads, including GPU clusters for computer vision models, media engines, and data analytics platforms 
  • Evolve our observability stack to proactively monitor system health, define meaningful alerting, and ensure high availability
  • Drive platform security and compliance through continuous vulnerability scanning, automated image screening, robust secrets management, and strict access controls
  • Collaborate closely with software engineers, data scientists, and product teams to design scalable architectures and act as a strategic technical partner for new infrastructure initiatives 

Help define technical direction, engineering best practices, and quality standards within the infrastructure domain 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 5+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Platform Engineering, with a proven track record of designing and scaling highly available production environments 
  • Strong hands-on experience running Kubernetes in production, including upgrades, networking and troubleshooting
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure (AWS) combined with experience operating bare-metal or self-hosted environments

Proven experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) and modern container build or GitOps workflowsStrong problem-solving skills and the ability to evaluate technical trade-offs between reliability, scalability, and maintainabilityExperience collaborating across engineering and product teams to deliver secure and robust infrastructure solutionsDeep understanding of Linux operating systems and strong programming or scripting skills (e.g., Python, Go, or Bash) focused on automation and tooling. 

Nice to have – and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience operating GPU workloads on Kubernetes or Machine Learning infrastructure
  • Familiarity with specialized Kubernetes ecosystem tools such as FluxCD, Rancher, or RKE2.
  • Experience working with large-scale video/streaming workflows or AWS media services
  • Experience managing and scaling messaging or event-streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) 
  • Experience operating and optimizing relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) 
  • Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling for engineering teams

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months time… You know our clusters and pipelines, handle incidents and upgrades on your own, and have shipped your first improvements to reliability, automation or security. You contribute confidently to architecture discussions.
  • In 12 months time… You own major parts of the platform, have delivered measurable improvements (faster deployments, better observability, stronger security), and help shape the roadmap of our hybrid cloud.

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet! 

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch! We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.

All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

jobs.title: Founding Engineer
jobs.description:
About Share

Share is a venture-backed startup building the global marketplace for bandwidth. We enable anyone to build their own programmable internet network, in seconds. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. Only the largest tech companies have escaped this, by spending billions to build their own physical networks. Share is giving that power to everyone.

Infrastructure providers sell their services in the Share Marketplace; giving builders, AI agents and enterprises the ability to build their own global backbone via an API layer. The path, the performance, how long they need it and paying only for what they use.


The role

We are hiring a Founding Engineer to take ownership of core platform architecture as we rebuild for a system roughly 50x the scale of what we had before. You'll design and scale distributed systems from scratch (this is deep systems-architecture work, not feature development on an existing system.) You will work directly with the Head of Development and a small team of engineers to ship production systems operating at global scale.

Non-negotiable

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with real, hands-on ownership of designing and scaling a production system from scratch. You can describe specific production incidents at scale (what broke, why, and what you changed) not just system-design-interview theory.

  • Deep TypeScript/Node.js expertise. You should be able to design a NestJS microservice from scratch, not just work in one.

  • Strong PostgreSQL skills. You can design schemas for complex, high-throughput production data, write migrations, and reason about transaction isolation and locking.

  • Experience with event-driven architectures (Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar). You understand the difference between request-reply and fire-and-forget patterns and when to use each.

  • You ship. You can take a spec document and turn it into production code without waiting for someone to break it into small tasks.

Nice to have, not required: prior fintech/payments experience or blockchain/distributed-ledger exposure

AI-augmented engineering (required mindset)

We expect every engineer at Share to use AI tools as a daily part of their workflow. This is how we operate. Our entire project planning, specification, and documentation process runs through AI-assisted sessions. Our codebase includes AI-readable context files. We use Claude for architecture decisions, code review, spec generation, and technical writing.

What this means for you:

  • You already use AI coding assistants (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) daily and can articulate how they change your workflow.

  • You are comfortable working with AI-generated specifications and can critically evaluate them, push back where they are wrong, and extend them where they are incomplete.

  • You see AI as a force multiplier that lets a small team operate at the capacity of a much larger one. You are not threatened by it; you are faster because of it.

  • You are willing to contribute to improving our AI-assisted workflows

Compensation & Details:

  • Competitive Salary & Equity package

  • Additional Benefits

  • Paid Business Travel when needed

  • Ownership in a venture-backed early stage startup building the future of physical and digital infrastructure in Africa

jobs.title: AI Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.

Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

 

How we work

  • Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

     

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

  • Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

  • AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

  • Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

     

What we look for

  • A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

  • Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

  • High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

  • Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

     

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

jobs.title: Photonic Component Modelling Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Salience Labs is building an industry-defining approach to optical circuit switching for AI infrastructure, engineered for real latency reduction and cost savings. We’re moving towards real-world deployment, and joining at this stage means genuine ownership over that next chapter, working alongside a highly technical team on one of the most consequential problems in AI infrastructure today.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Photonic Component Modelling Engineer to build and qualify behavioral and compact models that accurately capture the underlying device physics. Your models will be the foundation for system-level verification of systems that combine photonic and electronic components.

You’ll need to understand how a component’s behavior shifts with its surrounding optical and electrical circuitry and with operating conditions.

What You’ll Do

Working closely with the system verification, photonic design, and photonic characterization teams, you will:

  • Develop and maintain models of optical primitives (modulators, switches, photodetectors, couplers, etc.) for simulation and system verification environments

  • Verify that models accurately represent device physics across process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners

  • Release models that pass defined QA criteria

  • Verify PDK component libraries so that PDK updates and process variations don’t break circuit-level simulations

  • Extract model parameters from lab measurements and work with characterization to correlate simulation with measurement

  • Build and maintain automated tooling (Python and/or MATLAB) for parameter extraction, model fitting, and regression tracking

  • Maintain regression suites so model and PDK changes are checked against reference data before release

  • Resolve model discrepancies found at system level and feed model-based design risks back to photonic design

  • Keep reproducible records: version-controlled models, scripts, reference data, and QA results

What You Bring

Required

  • MS/PhD (or equivalent experience) in photonics, electrical engineering, applied physics, or a related field

  • 3+ years of experience in photonic component design and/or simulation

  • Solid understanding of integrated photonic building blocks, both passive and active, and their electrical drive requirements

  • Strong scripting ability (Python and/or MATLAB) for model fitting, data analysis, and simulation/measurement correlation

  • Comfortable working in Linux and with version-controlled repositories

  • Strong documentation habits, including model specifications, QA reports, and traceability from reference data to released models

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach across disciplines

Nice to have

  • Experience modelling signal propagation in photonic integrated circuits

  • Hands-on experience with silicon photonics platforms

  • Experience with optical/photonic simulation tools (e.g., FDTD, mode solvers, circuit-level simulators)

  • Familiarity with foundry PDK-based photonic design flows

  • Tcl scripting

Meet Arago and the Aragonians

Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors.

Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs.

Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles:

  1. Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to.

  2. High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time.

  3. One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie.

Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders.

What you’ll do

As a Senior Packaging Engineer, you will lead IC packaging initiatives from conceptualization and design to manufacturing process selection. You will establish the necessary supply chain, manage sub-contractors, and oversee the NPI and ramp-up phases for current and future Arago devices.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or Integrated Circuits Design.

  • 5+ years of experience in the semiconductor and photonic packaging industry.

  • Proficiency in heterogeneous integration and packaging processes, including wafer dicing (stealth, blade, diamond scribing), high-density Cu pillars and advanced bumping, flip-chip, redistribution layer and encapsulation (thermal lid, compression molding, glob-top), die attach and bonding techniques (epoxy, attach film, reflow, thermocompression, eutectic, laser-assisted bonding, Cu-Cu direct bonding), wirebonding, and 2.5D/3D integration schemes (back grinding, TSV reveal, die stacking, interposer).

We’re in our Munich office four days a week, with 100+ people building together every day. We measure outcomes. Trust is high and feedback is direct. We offer competitive salary and meaningful equity.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day.   • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

jobs.title: Builder
jobs.description:
Why this role exists

Manufacturing is Europe’s backbone, and it’s under pressure. More than half of manufacturing cost is decided in procurement, yet the function still runs on Excel.

Tacto is building the intelligence layer between bits and atoms, connecting the digital world of engineering with the physical world of manufacturing. It’s how AI gets into the real economy. More than 300 industrial companies already run on Tacto. We’re the category leader in DACH, backed by Sequoia and Index, and we’re just getting started.

 

What you'll do

Find the problems worth solving, then solve them end to end. Sit with buyers and procurement leads, work out what actually costs them money, decide what's worth building, and ship it to production, with AI doing much of the heavy lifting. You're done when it drives revenue, not when it's released. Don't wait for a PRD: make the case, or skip the case and show the prototype.

 

What we mean by Builder

Because of AI, we only hire Builders. No specialized roles. At Tacto, some of our Builders come from product, some from engineering, some from founding their own company. They all have one thing in common: they take a messy, unclear problem and own it from start to finish, whether it's a customer problem or a business problem. They decide what is worth doing, test the risky parts early, and see it through until it pays off. When it works, they share it, we double down, and everyone gets better.

We care about outcomes, not code quality for its own sake. What makes this fun is the loop from idea to reality, and AI just made that loop 10x shorter. There’s no room here for “my job is to solve interesting technical problems.”

 

What a week can look like

  • A call or a plant visit with a procurement team to see how they really buy

  • A prototype built with Claude Code or Cursor the next morning

  • Shipping with a team of 1-3 Builders on one of the quarter's bets

Who we're looking for

Hungry, creative people who care about the result more than anything else.

  • You've built something people used and owned the outcome: as a founder, in a fast-growing product team, or with a side project that you launched.

  • You have commercial sense and product taste. Agency and taste are the main differentiators in today's AGI age.

  • You build with AI every day. Cursor, Claude, Codex and agents are your default and you've made something real with them that wouldn't exist otherwise.

  • You have strong technical intuition: you reason about data and systems rather than getting caught up in the details of code.

  • You're comfortable in front of industrial customers. You are fluent in German; English is strong plus.

  • You want to be in a room full of people who are fired up about what they’re building.

  • Early in your career? Great. We love to bet on people with a steep learning curve.

 

How the process works

  1. Say Hello (20 min): get to know each other and the role

  2. Hiring Manager Interview (45 min)

  3. On-site day: a case with three Builders and Pool Leads (1 hour), Meet the Team (30 min)

How we work

We’re in our Munich office four days a week, with 100+ people building together every day. We measure outcomes. Trust is high and feedback is direct. We offer competitive salary and meaningful equity.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. This is a judgement role, not a filing one. Specifically, you will

• Vet the Skills Library and Legal Engineering outputs against the quality bar: review skills, workflows and use cases hands-on before they go live, and quality-control practice-area workflows for consistency.

• Research and experiment with prompting techniques, skill patterns and emerging AI methods, and turn what works into best practices the whole function adopts.

• Author the reference use cases that show what great looks like, published as the exemplars others copy.

• Work closely with the Product team on up-and-coming capabilities: early hands-on testing, the first best practices for new features, and structured feedback from real use.

• Produce materials that would support the technical onboarding and training for new Legal Engineers in your region, such as best practices to create use cases etc.

• Communicate new best practices, exemplars and platform changes to the Legal Engineering team worldwide.

• Support the flagship demos our CEO and C-suite take on stage at the industry’s biggest events: use case preparation, fixtures and rehearsal support.

• Oversee the quality and currency of the use case and skills libraries, including coordination across regions

• Spend roughly 30% of your time on live client work, selected for what it feeds back into the standards and libraries.

What you bring

You're a lawyer with real practice experience who has become genuinely technical: maybe you did a coding bootcamp, maybe you taught yourself, but either way you're the person colleagues ask how something actually works. You live in AI tools, and it shows: you can tell a strong use case from a plausible-sounding weak one, you know why a prompt underperforms before you've finished reading it, and you hold both halves of the judgement this role needs: what makes a prompt run well, and what makes a legal output substantively right rather than merely fluent. When you vet, you vet properly: line by line against the source, with the discipline to put the AI down when the job calls for your own eyes.

We're looking for

• A qualified lawyer with solid practice experience at a leading firm or in-house team, or equivalent: enough substantive judgement to vet outputs across practice areas.

• Real technical prowess: comfortable with code or scripting (a bootcamp or self-taught background counts entirely), and fluent in the mechanics of how AI tools actually behave.

• A heavy, habitual user of AI, ideally legal AI, with sharp prompt and use case discernment: able to rank a strong prompt against a mediocre one, articulate exactly why, and improve it.

• Visible pride in the craft of prompting and use case design: someone who wants to be the reference point for what good looks like.

• Rigour in review: line-by-line verification against source, and the judgement to know exactly when not to use AI.

• Comfortable running high-throughput workstreams: you triage well, keep many threads moving, and build process where volume demands it.

• Experience building skills, workflows or automations in a legal AI platform is a strong plus.

• Good to have: an M&A or wider transactional background, or deal coordination experience.

Where this role can go

This role is built to grow with the field itself. Applied legal AI knowledge barely exists as a discipline yet, and nobody accumulates evidence faster than the person vetting and testing the entire output of a global function. Do this job well and you are positioned to become one of the industry’s recognised voices on what good looks like. Inside Legora, the role is designed to grow into owning applied AI knowledge globally: the standards, techniques and systems every region operates on. If you've built something before, start here

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.

We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

  • Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

  • Document understanding: models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

  • Product matching: retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

  • Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

  • Training and serving infrastructure: automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

  • Customer problems: when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

  • A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

  • Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

  • You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

  • You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

  • You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

  • You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

  • You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

  • You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Our vision is to reimagine Relationship Banking for established SMEs, through the very best people, products and digital tools. We don’t pretend to have all the answers yet, and you will play a role in continuing to shape our offering.

Our Relationship Manager team was formed in 2022 and continues to grow with the Bank at pace. Providing every customer who opens an account with us with a Relationship Manager, to work alongside them and provide outstanding service, is core to our strategy.

In addition to providing outstanding service, our Relationship Managers build deep levels of understanding and trust with their customers, and get to understand their ambitions, goals and motivations. Allica Relationship Managers support their customers through the provision of appropriate Allica Bank products including Business Current Accounts, Savings Accounts, Commercial Loans, Asset Finance and Working Capital Facilities.

All Relationship Manager roles at Allica Bank carry a requirement for new business acquisition as we continue to build the bank. Where portfolios are held, they are built to allow capacity to do this. Relationship Managers will bring, and continue to build, a strong network of trusted SME advisors such as accountants, solicitors, business organisations and others (but not commercial finance brokers – these are looked after by our dedicated broker team). We expect our Relationship Managers to be recognised as valued partners and experts in business finance by their clients and in the communities they serve.

Principal Accountabilities

• Relationship Manage a portfolio of SME customers, understanding customer’s needs and business aspirations, and looking for opportunities to support them via Allica Bank services and through their own external networks

• Originating SME lending opportunities for both existing and new customers from initial enquiry through to completion, including writing credit papers in line with Allica’s credit policy and appetite.

• Delivering the business plan for your local area, and actively managing your objectives and personal development plan.

• Making your colleagues proud that you represent Allica in your local area, by ensuring excellent service for local SME customers, prospects and advisors.

• Working closely and collaboratively with all areas of Allica to ensure a seamless and professional service is always provided.

• Being a positive contributor to Allica’s culture, and always demonstrating the bank’s values

• Complying with all mandatory policies, and adherence to operational procedures to maintain internal controls.

Personal Attributes & Experience

• Highly capable Relationship Manager and Business Developer with a long-term track record of building high-value, trust based and long-lasting referral relationships.

• You will need to have a strong understanding of SME banking, which must include a background in commercial lending.

• You will be able to demonstrate a history of exemplary level of service, and of maximising the value with prospects and customers.

• You will be able to demonstrate a passion for SMEs, be a self-starter and bring an entrepreneurial mindset to your work.

• You will have excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with evidence of strong career progression and/or outperformance.

• You’ll be able to evidence an ability to work expertly with customers, colleagues and advisors to structure new lending proposals and write credit applications.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager (New Business)
jobs.description:
About Legal 500

Legal 500 is a global legal market research, data and intelligence business. Our research helps corporate clients make informed decisions about legal representation and gives law firms insight into their market position, performance, and clients.

Beyond research, we’re building a growing data, benchmarking, market-intelligence and subscription service offering. We bring the legal market together through a global programme of events - awards ceremonies, conferences and roundtables that convene leading law firms, in-house teams and their advisers. And through Legal Business, our journalistic title, we deliver independent news, analysis and commentary on the business of law and the strategy, performance and leadership of the world’s leading law firms.

We are a growing, multi-site organisation, with colleagues working across research, data, technology, product, journalism, commercial and events in London, Leeds and Bristol.

Our Rest of World New Business team launched in September and has been so successful that we are growing it. We are now looking for a Business Development Manager who loves winning new business and wants to build a pipeline across APAC, EMEA and the UK.

The role

You will own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and qualification through to negotiation and contract signature, selling subscription products on the Legal 500 platform to law firms of every size. Many of your leads will be warm, because firms already engage with our research process, but this is a hunter role: you will be on the phone, booking meetings, pitching and closing. You will speak with partners, senior lawyers, CMOs and marketing directors at some of the world's leading law firms, adapting your style to each market and audience.

The territory rotates through the year, giving you exposure to APAC, EMEA and the UK.

What you will do

  • Identify and target prospective law firm clients across the UK, APAC and EMEA.

  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline through calls, email, LinkedIn and face-to-face meetings.

  • Run compelling presentations and product demonstrations to senior decision makers.

  • Understand each firm's goals and align our subscription solutions to them.

  • Negotiate commercial terms and close deals to meet and exceed revenue targets.

  • Keep accurate CRM records and forecast your pipeline.

  • Share market intelligence with marketing, product and leadership, and work closely with customer success on handover.

What you will bring

  • At least 3 years of business development or new business sales experience, owning the full cycle from prospecting to close.

  • A track record of achieving or exceeding revenue targets.

  • Experience selling subscription, information, media, research or membership products, or other B2B sales to professional services firms.

  • Confidence engaging senior decision makers, including partners and C-suite.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills.

  • Resilience, drive and a proactive approach to picking up the phone.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling into law firms or other professional services.

  • A second language at business level.

  • Experience with Salesforce, HubSpot or Dynamics.

jobs.title: Enterprise AI Product Owner
jobs.description:
About Legal 500

Legal 500 is a global legal market research, data and intelligence business. Our research helps corporate clients make informed decisions about legal representation and gives law firms insight into their market position, performance, and clients.

Beyond research, we’re building a growing data, benchmarking, market-intelligence and subscription service offering. We bring the legal market together through a global programme of events - awards ceremonies, conferences and roundtables that convene leading law firms, in-house teams and their advisers. And through Legal Business, our journalistic title, we deliver independent news, analysis and commentary on the business of law and the strategy, performance and leadership of the world’s leading law firms.

We are a growing, multi-site organisation, with colleagues working across research, data, technology, product, journalism, commercial and events in London, Leeds and Bristol.

About the Role

Our new Enterprise AI Product Owner will own the adoption and value of AI in how Legal 500 works. You'll use our enterprise AI tools, with Microsoft Copilot and the wider Microsoft 365 AI capability as the main platform. You'll recommend what should be built or adopted and why, put governance in place where none yet exists, and make sure people across the business use the tools well.

This is a business-facing product role that starts from how the business works, not a technical build role. Copilot is the primary tool of choice, but you'll also oversee the other AI tools the business adopts.

What you'll do

You'll sit centrally within our People & Business Operations function, reporting to the Director of People & Business Operations. Your remit covers the whole of Legal 500, not a single department. You'll:

  • Own the roadmap and prioritised backlog for our enterprise AI opportunities, recommending what to build or adopt, what not to, and why. You'll write clear user stories and acceptance criteria and hold a consistent line with senior stakeholders when demand exceeds capacity.

  • Start every opportunity from the end-to-end business process. You'll walk business owners through how work gets done today, often where no SOPs exist, map the pain points, coach them through mapping a future-state process, and find where Copilot, other AI tools or workflow changes will make a measurable difference.

  • Personally configure, test and refine Copilot skills, agents and team workflows. You'll take ideas through proof of concept and pilot, then hand ownership of the output to the business owner.

  • Design, implement and enforce AI governance from the ground up. This includes owning the intake and review process for new use cases, agents and workflows, working alongside our Data Protection Officer, Information Security and IT Operations

  • Own our enterprise AI libraries: the register of approved tools and the libraries of approved agents, prompts, templates and shared workflows. You'll keep them curated, current and compliant, and avoid duplication between tools.

  • Design and deliver upskilling yourself, including training sessions, guides, clinics and self-serve resources. You'll also lead AI working groups and champion networks.

  • Spot common patterns across teams and bring them together on shared processes and solutions, so the same problem isn't solved many times.

  • Define and track adoption and value, such as usage, time saved, quality and user confidence. You'll maintain an AI benefits register, report progress to senior stakeholders and feed role impact into workforce planning.

What we're looking for

Essential

  • A process-led consulting approach, with a structured way of walking business owners through end-to-end processes, including where no SOPs existed

  • Proven experience of setting up AI governance from scratch and enforcing it. This includes owning an intake and review process and working with specialists such as a Data Protection Officer and IT Operations

  • Hands-on Microsoft Copilot experience: you've personally configured Copilot skills, agents or team workflows. Using Copilot, or overseeing someone else configuring it, isn't enough

  • Strong product management skills: setting priorities, writing user stories, running a backlog and managing senior stakeholders well

  • Experience of owning enterprise libraries or other centralised controls

  • Experience of running enablement yourself: you've designed and delivered upskilling personally, without relying on an L&D team, and you're comfortable leading working groups

Desirable

  • A genuine interest in enterprise efficiency and how people actually work, with a track record of bringing teams together on shared ways of working

  • A background in internal transformation, process improvement or Microsoft 365/Copilot SME roles, ideally including evaluating, onboarding or governing other enterprise AI tools

  • An understanding of professional services, publishing, legal markets or other knowledge-intensive environments

What this role isn't

  • It isn't about owning AI models in production, and working with development teams isn't the main job. There will be occasional technical work, but if you're mainly motivated by software delivery, this probably isn't the role for you

  • It isn't about running governance within someone else's framework, or handing enablement off to an L&D team. We need someone who has set these up and delivered them personally

Role information:

  • Hybrid workplace - 3 days a week in office, 2 days remote

  • This role can be based in either London or Leeds

  • Occasional travel to the other offices may be required (Bristol, London and Leeds)

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

Lendable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.

Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

  • Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider Lendable business

  • Keeping your knowledge of Lendable's products current through effective use and review of our policies, procedures and business tools

  • Turning your hand to other areas of operational need as the business requires

What we're looking for

  • Educated to degree level

  • Exceptional written communication - you can structure an argument and explain a complex decision clearly to someone who is not an expert

  • An aptitude for investigation, analysis, problem-solving and dispute resolution

  • Strong organisation and self-management - you can hold a caseload, prioritise it and work to deadlines without being chased

  • Sound judgment and a sound moral compass: willing to speak up to make sure good customer outcomes stay at the heart of what we do

  • Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced, changing environment

  • A willingness to learn FCA regulation and the DISP complaint handling rules and guidance

The interview process

We're not a corporation so we try our best to get things moving as quickly as possible. For this role we'd expect:

  • A 15 minute cognitive assessment

  • A quick phone call with one of the Talent team

  • An onsite assessment centre with a role focus and a final stage interview with the Complaints Management team to discuss your fit and capability for the role.

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

In Germany, home to the largest electricity market in Europe and a roadmap toward Net Zero by 2045, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. We are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As we expand our footprint in Germany and the wider European market, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and customer growth in Germany, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll work closely with our engineering team based in Manchester as we look to expand our engineering and operations in Germany and across Europe. Together, the team takes an integration project from the very early information stage, designs how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turns that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

The Gateway (Kraken’s IoT Edge Hardware & Software) and other connectivity technologies with their protocol engineering are owned by our UK-based team, who will support you in becoming configuration literate. Over time you will carry out configuration, deployments and testing for sites yourself, and feed back what you learn about hardware, connectivity and grid operator requirements for European countries so the wider team can build on it.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing, they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing ones.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches for German sites, mainly BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar). When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives in German and English through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Market access & prequalification support: Support the technical work needed for assets to enter ancillary-service markets (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) and to meet Redispatch 3.0 requirements. With guidance from senior engineers, help prepare the telemetry and control evidence for prequalification (Präqualifikation) with the relevant TSO. (Grid-code and plant-compliance obligations such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120 remain with the plant/PPC; our focus is enabling market access, telemetry and dispatch.)

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include German grid connection rules and TSO-specific requirements, ancillary services, Redispatch 3.0, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the Gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get Gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and software deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing of sites with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Hardware handling & dispatch: Berlin is planned as our stock base for our hardware going out to sites across Europe, so the role includes some hands-on work. This covers preparing units before they ship, such as flashing and configuring our industrial PCs and running pre-shipment tests, and helping to prepare and coordinate shipments.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning, initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand in Germany and other parts of Europe grows. Hardware is deployed remotely in most cases via O&Ms and third parties, but occasional hands-on support in Germany may be needed before or after a deployment.

  • Incidents & support: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Language: Native or professional fluency in German and English, needed for technical documentation and for working with customers, grid operators and our UK-based team.

  • Understanding of the German connection landscape: Working knowledge of the TSO/DSO hierarchy, the connection/integration process, and the technical connection rules (such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120) a grid-connected asset must meet before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the German energy markets: Working understanding of the German ancillary services (FCR, aFRR, mFRR), what prequalification involves, and the Redispatch 3.0 framework.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Hands-on hardware preparation: Comfortable working at the bench with our panels and industrial PCs. This includes safely powering panels up and down using our test setup, flashing operating system images, and following a set procedure for pre-shipment checks. Full training is provided.

  • Industrial communication protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, diagrams and tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with a team that is partly based in another country.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Location and travel: Ideally based close to Kraken’s Berlin office. Willingness to travel to customers and sites in Germany, and occasionally to our Manchester team, although travel is kept to a minimum. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of German grid compliance (VDE-AR-N 4110/4120, TSO-specific technical requirements) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (NIS2, EnWG/KRITIS awareness; IEC 62443 a plus).

  • Exposure to the wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks beyond Germany.

jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken Customer

 

What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

 

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

 

🏠 Where you'll fit in:

 

We’re looking for a brilliant senior Data & Analytics Client Delivery Lead to help clients fully leverage Kraken data and transform their data team and capabilities. You should bring extensive experience doing analytics on a strong, modern data team (e.g., data analytics, business intelligence, or related field -- analytics manager, lead data analyst, analytics or data consultant or similar); a love of working with clients; and a passion for driving the clean energy transition – energy sector experience is a plus!

 

The role

 

You’ll work directly with Kraken clients to help them develop modern, transformative data and analytics capabilities as part of their broader Kraken transformation. You’ll train them on Kraken data and support them in building critical reporting & insightful analytics, sometimes getting hands-on with query writing or demo analytics. 

 

You’ll also leverage your experience leading strong analytics teams to advise senior client data leadership on how to build a high-performing, business-centric data organization and leverage data as a strategic asset to unlock ambitious business and clean energy goals.

 

We are a flat and agile organisation and plan to remain this way. We are looking for a hands-on Data & Analytics Client Delivery Lead that can support both directly and indirectly - sometimes jumping in and writing queries or solving data challenges and other times advising or upskilling both clients and colleagues. 

 

You will play a critical role in ensuring the clients’ reporting and analytics transition to Kraken goes smoothly - and ensuring that clients build the transformative data capabilities needed to get full value from Kraken data and power aspirational business goals.

🚀 What you'll own:

  • Guide clients in redefining critical reporting and analytics to use new Kraken data and concepts, through hands-on query writing, working sessions, and trainings

  • Advise clients, including senior leadership, on topics like how to develop a high-performing data organization, how to build a modern tech stack, and how to pursue a data strategy and priorities that drive their core business objectives.

  • Strategically define and prioritize client data needs to influence the data product roadmap, ensuring product understands the core, shared client needs and that solutions achieve clients’ desired business outcomes

  • Partner with engineering to deliver new data features and requirements aligned to client use cases

  • Train Kraken’s broader client delivery team on how to help their respective business domains ask effective data questions and leverage data directly to drive business impact

🧠 What you’ll bring to the party:

  • Degree qualified equivalent, with strong client delivery and/or product ownership experience

  • Several years of experience as a data analytics, business intelligence, or related field -- analytics manager, lead data analyst, analytics or data consultant or similar

  • Strong familiarity with modern data practices and tools

  • Strong facility with SQL and modern BI toolsFamiliar with agile product development practices and experience collaborating with engineering

  • Excellent communications, collaboration and presentation skills

  • Strong influencing skills and ability to challenge traditional ways of thinking

  • Patience – our clients are undergoing huge transformations that take time and require our understanding

  • Experience in the energy sector a plus

jobs.title: Consultant déploiement ERP (H/F)
jobs.description: Vous souhaitez accompagner le déploiement d'un ERP au sein d'un groupe à dimension internationale et intervenir au cœur des enjeux opérationnels de ses différentes filiales ?  Dans le cadre du renforcement de ses équipes, nous recherchons un(e) Consultant(e) ERP Déploiement pour accompagner l'intégration et l'évolution de la solution ERP du Groupe auprès de ses entités en France et à l'international. CLIENT FINALEn lien étroit avec les équipes métiers, les managers de filiales et les équipes informatiques, vous serez un interlocuteur clé dans le déploiement de l'ERP.  Vous interviendrez sur l'ensemble des étapes du déploiement, de l'analyse des processus métiers jusqu'à la formation et l'accompagnement des utilisateurs :  * Analyser les processus métiers et les flux opérationnels des filiales afin de comprendre leurs besoins et leurs spécificités locales.  * Identifier les écarts entre les pratiques métiers existantes et les fonctionnalités proposées par l'ERP, puis formaliser les besoins et les demandes d'évolution.  * Participer au paramétrage de la solution, aux phases de tests et à la validation des fonctionnalités, en lien avec les équipes internes.  * Piloter et coordonner les différentes étapes des projets de déploiement : planification, suivi des actions, gestion des échéances et identification des risques.  * Animer des réunions et des ateliers avec les différents interlocuteurs afin de faire avancer les sujets et garantir une bonne coordination entre les équipes.  * Préparer et accompagner les utilisateurs clés dans les phases de recette et de validation de la solution.  * Former les utilisateurs finaux et les accompagner dans la prise en main de l'ERP, en tenant compte de leurs métiers et de leurs besoins.  * Assurer un reporting régulier auprès de votre responsable, remonter les alertes et veiller au respect des plans d'action.  Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes métiers et informatiques du Groupe, dans un environnement international impliquant des échanges réguliers en anglais avec les filiales.  Des déplacements à l'international sont à prévoir selon les projets, avec des durées et des fréquences variables. Contrat : CDI Salaire : 40/45K€ selon expérience Télétravail : 1 jour par semaineDe formation supérieure, vous disposez idéalement d'une première expérience dans un environnement métier (ADV, production, logistique, gestion des flux.) et avez développé une appétence pour la gestion de projets, la coordination ou l'accompagnement au changement.  Une expérience en tant que key user ou dans le cadre d'un projet de déploiement d'ERP constitue un véritable atout.  Vous possédez les qualités et compétences suivantes :  * Bonne compréhension des processus métiers et des flux opérationnels.  * Capacité à recueillir, analyser et synthétiser les besoins des utilisateurs.  * Aisance dans la coordination de projets transverses et le suivi de plans d'action.  * Bon relationnel et capacité à échanger avec des interlocuteurs variés, métiers comme techniques. * Esprit de synthèse, réactivité et capacité à alerter et relancer les bons interlocuteurs pour faire avancer les sujets.  * Goût pour la transmission et capacité à accompagner et former les utilisateurs.  * Anglais professionnel indispensable, à l'écrit comme à l'oral. La maîtrise d'une troisième langue, notamment l'allemand, l'espagnol ou l'italien, sera particulièrement appréciée.  Au-delà de votre parcours, nous recherchons une personne curieuse, impliquée et dotée d'un excellent relationnel, qui aime comprendre le fonctionnement d'une entreprise, créer du lien entre les équipes et faire avancer les projets jusqu'à leur aboutissement. Process de recrutement  - Un premier échange avec notre cabinet, si nous n'avons pas déjà eu l'occasion de nous rencontrer.  - Un premier entretien avec notre client.  - Un ou plusieurs échanges complémentaires avec les équipes internes.  Vous souhaitez évoluer au cœur des projets de transformation d'un groupe international et contribuer concrètement à l'harmonisation de ses processus métiers ? Contactez moi pour en discuter !

jobs.title: Tegevusjuhendaja
jobs.description:

Tööülesanded: Oled hooliv, vastutustundlik ning hindad meeskonnatööd ja arengut? Siis on see ametikoht Sulle! Sinu töö eesmärgiks on arendada ja säilitada psüühilise erivajadusega inimeste elukvaliteeti. Selleks tuleb igapäevaselt kliendiga koos või tema jaoks teha erinevaid tegevusi: - iseseisvalt elamiseks vajalike oskuste õpetamine; - tööalane nõustamine; - vajadusel arsti külastamine; - juhendamine kodu korrashoiul ja toitumisel; - suhtlemine kliendi lähedastega; - dokumentide haldamine; - vaba aja sisustamise motiveerimine või juhendamine; - võrgustiku- ja meeskonnatöö korraldamine. Kliendiga tehtud töö tuleb dokumenteerida ning see võtab umbes pool tööajast. Töö nõuab tahtmist ja võimekust ringi liikuda - korterite külastused, arstil, tööandja juures käimised jms. Teenusel olevatele inimestele väljasõitude ja ühisürituste korraldamine ja nendel osalemine. Tööle asudes tuleb arvestada, et osa väljaõppest toimub Tartus.

Omalt poolt pakume: Meil on hooliv ja kokkuhoidev kollektiiv - jagame ühiselt nii muresid kui rõõme. Elvas on kokkuhoidev kollektiiv. Kord kuus toimuvad asutuse töökoosolekud Tartus. Uutele töötajatele toimuvad uue töötaja koolitused, kus kõik erialaga seotud teemad detailselt läbi käime. Lisaks on olemas mentori ja kvaliteedijuhi tugi. Võid kindel olla, et see ametikoht arendab Sind. Töö pakub võimalust tunda end vajaliku ja olulisena. Tööalaste väljakutsetega toimetulekuks toimuvad regulaarsed kovisioonid ja supervisioonid. Pakume puhkust suveperioodil ja tasustatud lisapuhkepäevi jõulude ajal ning tasustatud vaba päeva võimalust. Toimuvad ühised väljasõidud õppimise- ja kogemuste saamise eesmärgil. Sul on töö tegemiseks oma kindel töökoht, arvuti ja töö telefoniga. Juhul kui erialane haridus puudub, on võimalik see omandada tööl käimise ajal.

Muud nõuded: Töö edukaks elluviimiseks on vaja järgmisi omadusi: hoolivus, sallivus, vastutustunne, asjatundlikkus, avatus, uuendusmeelsus. Sul peab olema valmisolek tööks puuetega inimestega - võimekus toime tulla pingelistes olukordades, kus on vaja rahu säilitada. Väga oluline on iseenda tundmine, võimekus hoida oma vaimset tervist korras. Samuti on vaja osata oma tööd ja tööaega planeerida. Töö eeldab võimekust töötada nii individuaalselt kui meeskonnas. Silluste ehitus sarrusplokist: paigaldus, armeerimine, valamine ja ajutine toestus. Ehitaja peab arvestama tugipindade, koormuste ja toestuse eemaldamise ajaga. Akende puhul valmistab ehitaja ette avad ning teeb paigaldussõlme tihenduse ja liitumise seina soojustuse ja tõketega. Aknad paigaldab tootja meeskond. Vaheseinte ehitus: karkass, soojustus ja kipsplaat. Ehitaja arvestab heli- ja tuleohutusnõuetega ning eriosade läbiviikude ja kinnituste asukohtadega. Eriosade paigaldustööd Veetorustiku, kütte- ja jahutustorustiku ning ventilatsioonitorustiku paigaldus eriosade projektide järgi. Ehitaja hoiab kalded, kinnitused ja isolatsiooni korras ning koordineerib tööd teiste osapooltega. Survekatsete läbiviimine ja tulemuste fikseerimine protokollis. Lisaks ootame Kaetud tööde ettevalmistamist ülevaatuseks ja osalemist nende dokumenteerimisel. Oma töö kvaliteedi kontrolli enne järgmise etapi algust. Võimet märgata jooniste ebakõlasid ja anda neist objektijuhile õigeaegselt teada.
